creative.central_question: How do you know a change to your skill, agent or MCP tool actually helped?
creative.payoff: Rerun the same eval after every customization change and compare the runs; it is in public preview.
creative.visual_motif: The signal trace: one task goes through the agent twice; the first trace ends in a green check, the rerun forks to a red one; later before/after eval runs sit side by side.
creative.music: none (voice only for this dry run)

scenes.narration: One good answer doesn't prove your skill works.
scenes.motion: headline words punch in on voice stress; a cyan trace dot enters from the left and lands on a mint check; slow 3% push-in
scenes.visual_description: Headline in the question zone; below it a single cyan trace ending in a green check on the dark gradient.

scenes.narration: AI output can change from one run to the next. You edit a skill, try it once, and it passes.
scenes.motion: amber task chip enters; trace dot travels task -> agent -> output; output node changes label as the run repeats; mint check lights at the end
scenes.visual_description: Vertical flow of three generic labelled nodes (Task, Agent, Output) with the motif trace; amber task chip, mint pass check.

scenes.narration: Rerun it, and it fails. So how do you know your change helped?
scenes.motion: same trace runs in both halves; left ends in mint check, right forks to a coral cross; question mark pulses in the pinned headline
scenes.visual_description: Two stacked halves labelled Run 1 and Run 2 (illustrative); pinned question headline stays visible.

scenes.narration: An eval is a repeatable test for AI behavior.
scenes.motion: the two traces merge into one loop; step tag 1/3 2/3 3/3 pips draw on under the title
scenes.visual_description: Title text with three empty step pips and a looping cyan trace; no vendor logo.

scenes.narration: Step one: give an agent a realistic task, and describe a good result.
scenes.motion: amber task node draws on, then a mint 'good result' checklist node; arrow links them as each is named; pip 1/3 fills
scenes.visual_description: Two labelled nodes: Task (amber) and Good result (mint) connected by a cyan arrow.

nodes.label: What a good result looks like

scenes.narration: Step two: approve the run and see which checks passed and failed.
scenes.motion: own unbranded approve button taps, then checklist rows resolve one by one into mint passes and one coral fail; pip 2/3 fills
scenes.visual_description: Generic card with an Approve button and four check rows; rows turn mint or coral. Own mock, not a vendor UI. Result rows carry an on-screen 'Illustrative' label.

scenes.narration: Step three: change your skill, agent or MCP tool, and compare before and after.
scenes.motion: trace loops Eval -> Edit -> Eval; two result tiles (before, after) slide together at the end; pip 3/3 fills
scenes.visual_description: Cycle of three generic nodes (Eval, Edit, Eval) with the motif trace; before and after result tiles at the bottom.

scenes.narration: Illustrative: your edit passed by hand, but the rerun shows a failed check.
scenes.motion: left tile 'by hand' shows mint check; right tile 'eval rerun' shows rows with one coral fail that pulses once; ILLUSTRATIVE badge stays on
scenes.visual_description: Before/after halves; left mint, right coral; prominent 'Illustrative' badge, no real numbers.

scenes.narration: So rerun the same eval after every change, and compare the runs. It's in public preview.
scenes.visual_description: Callback to the hook trace, now looping through layered before/after run tiles; a small coral 'Public preview' caveat chip with source chip at the bottom.
scenes.visual_justification: Depth separates the before-run and after-run layers of the same trace so the comparison reads at a glance.
scenes.motion: foreground and background tile layers drift at different speeds; the trace returns from the hook and completes the loop; caveat chip fades in on 'public preview'

scenes.narration: Which skill would you test first? Tell me below.
scenes.motion: question types on; trace dot circles back toward the start so the last frame can loop to the hook
scenes.visual_description: Clean end card with the question; trace dot positioned to loop into scene 1.
